Consequently, all output elements are computed from batch 0 only, causing ~94% mismatch (all batches except batch 0). The repeat_interleave kernel is likely correct for the model's dim=1 usage, but its grid-stride loop only processes a subset of the huge output (67 million elements) when the grid is capped at 65535, leaving many output elements uninitialized. We must fix both kernels and launchers to correctly pass and use b, c, l_in, and l_out, and to implement proper grid-stride loops covering all output elements. Additionally, the binding for repeat_interleave_like allocates output with shape [batch, repeats, channels, length] and then flattens it; this is correct only if the launcher writes in contiguous order, which it does with src_idx = i % input_size, producing exact repetition of the entire flattened input. We must ensure the grid-stride loop covers all output elements and uses 64-bit indexing.
